title: Choose the new Orangutan Adventure Sumatra world
question: I recommend a field-expedition system that turns trek comparison into a clear route through forest, camp, and river. Keep it, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Forest Transect
options.lineage: rainforest survey plots, trail tags, waterproof route charts
options.body: Deep canopy photography leads. Numbered field markers, contour lines, safety-tape colors, and a continuous trek route organize packages, ethics, guides, camp, and river return. The first viewport feels like arriving at the trailhead with Syaipul, not browsing a tour catalog. Risk: field notation must stay human and never become technical clutter.

options.label: River Line
options.lineage: midnight enamel transit diagram fused with jungle routes
options.body: Every trek becomes a colored line with stations for habitat, camp nights, and river return. Exceptionally clear for comparison and trip planning, but its urban transport grammar is less rooted in Bukit Lawang.

options.label: Canopy Glass
options.lineage: hand-rolled glass partition fused with a documentary photo wall
options.body: A black glazing grid frames real people, wildlife, and trip proof in clear, seeded, amber, and cobalt panes. It is visually distinctive and image-led, but carries less of the route-planning mechanism.
